gap: No result ChatGPT got states the maker-store price per inch of screen for kits that include a rear camera ($8.57/in for the HIEHA 7-inch up to $32.03/in for the Carpuride W103 Pro), or that the Carpuride 9–10.3-inch units take only 12.5 W over USB-C (5 V × 2.5 A).
standout_why: I compared against cartechtalk.com (IIWEY iK7 $139.99, Krunia $89.99, HAUXIY Q9S $84.99 with a 7 m cable) and gearnudge.com (Carpuride C3/C92/C98/W103 Pro prices, plus a general note that standard kits 'usually come with about 32.8 feet of cable' and that large trucks or three-row SUVs may need an extension). Both give prices and gearnudge covers the cable-reach question in general terms. Neither gives a price per inch or a power draw for any unit. Still, price per inch and a 12.5 W draw only add a little to prices both pages already show.
decides: This confirms the pick more than it changes it. Measured by price per inch with a rear camera in the box, the HIEHA 7-inch ($59.99, 1080P camera included) and the ESSGOO 1026SCP ($119.99 at essgoo.com, 10.26 in) cost far less than Carpuride's W103 line ($29–32 per inch). So the shopper pays almost 3 times as much per inch for the Carpuride brand. The angle that would really decide this, whether the bundled camera cable reaches the back of a long truck or SUV, I could not derive. I could not open any maker page that gives the bundled cable length for the ESSGOO, Easyonlife or Carpuride screens.
